briefings.title: AI Is Writing the Code Now: Cisco’s Vision for the Agent Era

people.name: Jeetu Patel
people.role: EVP and Chief Product Officer, Cisco

briefings.tldr: Cisco is transitioning to an "Agent Era" where AI acts as an autonomous co-worker rather than just a tool, with plans to have 60–70% of its entire product portfolio written by AI by the end of 2027.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Cisco is transitioning to an "Agent Era" where AI acts as an autonomous co-worker rather than just a tool, with plans to have 60–70% of its entire product portfolio written by AI by the end of 2027. This shift demands a new focus on agent-specific security and a heterogeneous infrastructure strategy that revitalizes the role of the CPU alongside GPUs.

## The Evolution of AI-Generated Engineering
* **Product Roadmap:** Jeetu Patel revealed that Cisco’s "AI Defense" is their first product 100% written by AI.
    * By the end of 2026, Cisco expects to have a half-dozen products written entirely by AI.
    * By the end of 2027, the goal is for 60% to 70% of the entire portfolio to be AI-generated.
* **Redefining Engineering Roles:** Writing code currently only accounts for 30–35% of an engineer's time. AI will handle the "plumbing," allowing humans to focus on higher-level architecture, problem-solving, and judgment.
* **The New Scrum Team:** Patel predicts a fundamental shift in team structure. A traditional eight-person scrum team will evolve into a team of two humans managing six AI agents.

## Infrastructure: The Renaissance of the CPU and the Edge
* **Heterogeneous Compute:** While the initial AI wave focused almost exclusively on GPUs, the "Agent Era" requires a mix of GPUs, accelerators, and CPUs.
* **CPU Resurgence:** CPUs are seeing a "renaissance" because they are superior for the orchestration required by complex AI agents. Patel noted that the market for high-performance CPUs is currently "on fire."
* **Token Generation at the Edge:** Cisco is pushing for AI processing to move out of the data center and toward the edge.
    * **Unified Edge:** Cisco is integrating the Nvidia Spectrum 4500 chip into its unified edge platforms to allow for simple, plug-and-play AI deployment in branch offices that lack dedicated IT support.

## Security and Trust in the Agent Era
* **Agent Security as an Industry:** Patel identifies agent security as a massive emerging sector. Unlike traditional security, which was the primary concern of the CISO, agent security impacts every user directly.
* **The Trust Gap:** Currently, many enterprises are running agents on isolated hardware (like Mac Minis) because they do not yet trust agents on their main production networks. 
* **Dynamic Guardrails:** As agents become more autonomous, security must move from static rules to dynamic guardrails that can prevent an agent from making catastrophic errors, such as accidentally deleting production databases.

## Key Announcements at GTC 2026
* **AI Networking:** Cisco announced support for Nvidia’s Spectrum 4 and Spectrum 6 (the 100-terabit chip), providing customers with more choice in high-speed networking fabrics.
* **HyperShield & BlueField:** Cisco’s HyperShield (a hybrid mesh firewall) will now support Nvidia BlueField DPUs.
* **AI Defense Integration:** Cisco is positioning its AI Defense product to secure the specific agent-based technologies being released by Nvidia.

## Notable Quotes
> "A scrum team in the future will no longer look like eight people; it'll look like two people and six agents. And you will have four scrum teams for every scrum team you have right now." — **Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco**

> "You have to assume that whatever deficiencies you have in these models right now... by the time you actually get yourself prepared to take advantage of them, they will be solved. You have to fast forward three to six months." — **Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco**

> "Agent security is going to be a huge industry moving forward... because something going sideways with an agent would actually have meaningful consequence to the user using it." — **Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco**

> "There are no priors to AI. It’s too fast. It’s happening too fast and I do think there’s going to be disruption that we’re going to have to collectively make sure that you actually think through." — **Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco**

briefings.title: China Global Podcast - Ep 121 ft. Da Wei
briefings.channel: The German Marshall Fund of the United States

people.name: Da Wei
people.role: Director, Center for International Strategy and Security, Tsinghua University

briefings.tldr: The upcoming March 31–April 2 summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping aims to stabilize a "stable but distracted" relationship through major trade purchases (soybeans, Boeing aircraft), though significant geopolitical breakthroughs on Taiwan or Iran are unlikely due to late planning and misaligned strategic goals.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** The upcoming March 31–April 2 summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping aims to stabilize a "stable but distracted" relationship through major trade purchases (soybeans, Boeing aircraft), though significant geopolitical breakthroughs on Taiwan or Iran are unlikely due to late planning and misaligned strategic goals.

## Strategic Climate and Economic Leverage
*   **State of Relations:** Dr. Da Wei characterizes the current relationship as stable but notes that the Trump administration is currently distracted by conflicts in the Middle East (Iran), Venezuela, and Greenland.
*   **Perception of U.S. Power:**
    *   **Leadership vs. Resources:** While the U.S. remains the most powerful nation technologically and militarily, its global leadership is declining because it is "undermining the institutions it set up after WWII."
    *   **Strategic Assessment:** Chinese scholars are debating whether U.S. military actions in Iran and Venezuela signal a reversal of U.S. decline, but no consensus exists.
*   **Economic "Nuclear Weapons":**
    *   **Mutual Assured Disruption:** Both nations use specific dependencies as leverage. The U.S. utilizes chips and high-tech restrictions, while China utilizes rare earth elements.
    *   **Self-Defense Motive:** Da Wei asserts that China’s use of leverage is defensive—intended to limit damage caused by U.S. policy—rather than offensive (e.g., China has pointedly chosen not to provide military aid to Russia or Iran).

## Economic Deliverables and Trade Friction
*   **U.S. Objectives:** President Trump is expected to seek massive purchase agreements to reduce the trade deficit and secure mineral supply chains.
    *   **Commodities:** Large-scale purchases of U.S. soybeans.
    *   **Aviation:** Potential deals for up to 500 Boeing aircraft.
    *   **Critical Minerals:** Ensuring smoother flows of rare earths, which have seen shortages affecting U.S. defense and tech sectors.
*   **Beijing’s Objectives:**
    *   **Tariff Predictability:** China seeks a long-term solution to Section 301 and 232 tariffs rather than short-term renewals, which create business uncertainty.
    *   **Investment "White Lists":** Beijing is interested in agreements that would allow Chinese companies to invest in specific U.S. sectors to create jobs and balance trade.
    *   **Reciprocity in Tech:** If China purchases Boeing planes, it wants the U.S. to stop restricting parts for China’s domestic C919 aircraft.

## Geopolitics: Taiwan and the "One China" Policy
*   **Arms Sales as a Red Line:** China is deeply concerned about U.S. arms sales to Taiwan. 
    *   Following an $11 billion package earlier this year, reports of a potential $20 billion package caused Beijing to warn that such a move could cancel future summits.
    *   Trump’s decision to postpone the package is viewed by Beijing as a "smart decision" to preserve the March summit.
*   **Potential for a "New Deal":**
    *   **Transactional Diplomacy:** Da Wei suggests that because President Trump is "transactional" and lacks the rigid ideological beliefs of his predecessors regarding Taiwan, there is a unique opportunity to "think outside the box."
    *   **Rethinking Ambiguity:** Beijing wants the U.S. to move from "not supporting" Taiwan independence to actively "opposing" it, arguing that the 70-year-old policy of strategic ambiguity is increasingly dangerous.

## Global Conflicts and Internal PLA Dynamics
*   **The Iran Conflict:** 
    *   **Limited Cooperation:** China views U.S. and Israeli actions against Iran as "unlawful" and will not take any action that appears to support the U.S. coalition (e.g., pressuring Iran or joining naval escorts in the Strait of Hormuz).
    *   **Summit Impact:** The most optimistic outcome is a high-level joint statement calling for peace and de-escalation, intended to prevent the Iran issue from undermining the bilateral summit.
*   **PLA Purges and Stability:**
    *   **Xi’s Command:** Recent investigations and removals of high-ranking Chinese military officers are described as an anti-corruption campaign that does not affect China's strategic direction.
    *   **Operational Control:** Strategic decisions regarding the U.S. and Taiwan are made exclusively by Xi Jinping; therefore, internal military churn will not impact the summit or cross-strait stability.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I think the if we are discussing the power, the hegemony, the leadership of the US, I think it's basically lies in the international institutions that US led after the World War II... From that regard, I think US is declining, because the US is destroying or kind of undermining the institution that it set up." — **Dr. Da Wei**

> "I call it [rare earths] economic nuclear weapon. So it some people say mutual assured disruption in economic field, like the nuclear weapon as a mutual assured destruction in military field." — **Dr. Da Wei**

> "President Trump is really hard to predict... He is a transactional president, want to do some deal. So I think that's an opportunity for the two sides to think something new [regarding Taiwan]." — **Dr. Da Wei**

briefings.title: Creating prediction markets (and suing the CFTC) with Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara
briefings.tldr: Kalshi is the first federally regulated prediction market in the US, achieving 11x volume growth in six months ($10.4B in February 2024) after successfully suing its own regulator, the CFTC, to permit election markets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Kalshi is the first federally regulated prediction market in the US, achieving 11x volume growth in six months ($10.4B in February 2024) after successfully suing its own regulator, the CFTC, to permit election markets. By leveraging a decentralized network of "super-forecasters" rather than traditional institutions, Kalshi is evolving from a binary "yes/no" platform into a full-scale financial exchange for non-traditional commodities like GPU compute and weather events.

## Regulatory Strategy and the CFTC Lawsuit
* **"Permission First" Philosophy:** Unlike the traditional Silicon Valley "ask for forgiveness" model (e.g., Uber, PayPal), co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara pursued a regulatory-first approach, spending four years securing CFTC approval before launching.
    * **The "Pocket Veto":** In late 2022, the CFTC delayed election market approval, leading to significant layoffs and a collapse in investor morale. 
* **Suing the Regulator:** In a rare "anti-pattern" for a 25-person startup, Kalshi sued the CFTC in 2023 after the agency blocked election contracts for a second time. 
    * **The Legal Basis:** The court ruled that elections have clear economic impacts and do not fall under prohibited categories like war, terrorism, or assassination.
    * **Outcome:** The victory allowed Kalshi to list 2024 election markets, which became a primary driver for mainstream adoption and institutional credibility.

## Market Mechanics and Participant Profiles
* **The 95/5 Liquidity Split:** Contrary to rumors of "Jane Street" dominance, less than 5% of Kalshi's maker orders come from large institutional market makers.
    * **"Internet Anons":** Over 95% of liquidity is provided by individuals and small "garage" shops (roughly 2,000 active full-time entities) who monitor specialized situations in real-time.
* **Super-Forecasters vs. Experts:** Kalshi’s most accurate data often comes from non-traditional sources.
    * **Case Study:** The platform’s top inflation forecaster is a resident of Kansas with no prior financial background who simply "feels" the data through obsessive news consumption.
    * **Niche Monetization:** An Ariana Grande super-fan profited $150,000 by trading on music chart rankings, using the proceeds to pay off student loans and buy a car.
* **Incentive Engineering:** Kalshi uses fee structures to incentivize "pro-social" market behavior, rewarding those who provide stable liquidity during volatile events (like touchdowns or breaking news) to prevent spreads from blowing out.

## Hyper-Growth and Product Roadmap
* **Growth Numbers:** Volume reached $10.4B in February 2024, representing an 11x increase over six months.
* **The Four Pillars of Expansion:** To become the "biggest derivatives exchange in the world," Mansour and Lopes Lara are focused on:
    * **Breadth of Topics:** Moving from politics and sports into "commodities of the future" like GPU compute and shipments.
    * **Market Structure:** Transitioning from simple binary (Yes/No) contracts to complex futures, swaps, and options.
    * **Margining Systems:** Moving away from 100% upfront capital requirements to allow for more capital-efficient hedging on long-term events (e.g., hurricane insurance).
    * **Distribution:** Expanding the "broker mix" through partners like Robinhood and Interactive Brokers to reach retail and international users.

## Social Impact: An Antidote to Polarization
* **Truth Incentives:** Prediction markets are presented as a corrective to algorithmic social media feeds. While social media rewards engagement and "rabbit holes," Kalshi rewards accuracy and "skin in the game."
* **The "Iowa/New Hampshire" Effect:** Prediction markets create a real-time narrative based on probability rather than punditry. This provides a faster feedback loop for policymakers to understand how specific messages or events are actually resonating with the public.
* **Insider Trading Policy:** Kalshi maintains a strict surveillance division to flag trades based on confidential data. 
    * **Stricter than SEC:** While members of Congress can legally trade stocks, Kalshi prohibits them from trading on political contracts related to their own legislative work.

> "We wanted to build the next generation New York Stock Exchange. We wanted to build a financial market that is in the US, that is credible, that is regulated. We were not very excited about this idea of building something offshore." — **Tarek Mansour**

> "The law applies to companies, but it also applies to the government... The lawsuit told the CFTC that they couldn't just do whatever they wanted." — **Luana Lopes Lara**

> "The incentive structure for a prediction market is truth. It is more volume, it is more liquidity, which translates to a better and a more accurate forecast." — **Tarek Mansour**

briefings.title: Greetings, Earthlings: Philip Johnston of Starcloud on Data Centers in Space
briefings.tldr: Starcloud is migrating AI compute to space to bypass terrestrial energy and land constraints, leveraging plummeting launch costs and superior solar efficiency to make space-based data centers the primary infrastructure for AI inference within the next decade.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Starcloud is migrating AI compute to space to bypass terrestrial energy and land constraints, leveraging plummeting launch costs and superior solar efficiency to make space-based data centers the primary infrastructure for AI inference within the next decade.

## The Economic and Logistical Case for Space
*   **Terrestrial Bottlenecks:** Building 100MW+ energy projects on Earth currently faces 5-10 year lead times due to permitting, regulatory hurdles, and land scarcity.
*   **Solar Efficiency:** Space-based solar provides **8x the energy** of terrestrial solar per square meter because it lacks atmospheric interference and operates in 24/7 sunlight, eliminating the need for expensive battery storage.
*   **Cost Break-even:** Philip Johnston estimates the breakeven point for space-based compute is a launch cost of **$500/kg**. As terrestrial land and power costs rise, this threshold may shift closer to $1,000/kg. 
*   **Marginal Cost Dynamics:** Unlike Earth, where the marginal cost of each additional data center increases due to grid strain, space-based infrastructure costs decrease at scale through mass manufacturing and reusable launch vehicles.

## Technical Engineering and Maintenance
*   **The Heat Dissipation Problem:** Because a vacuum acts as an insulator, traditional convection cooling is impossible. Starcloud uses infrared radiation and "phase change" materials to manage thermals.
    *   **Advanced Radiators:** Next-generation satellites (Starcloud 2) will feature large deployable radiators using liquid cooling loops and heat pumps to artificially boost radiator temperature for better dissipation.
*   **Radiation Resilience:** To combat bit-flips and hardware degradation, Starcloud conducts extensive testing at particle accelerators (e.g., Brookhaven National Lab) to simulate five years of radiation in 24 hours.
*   **Hardware Longevity:** The company targets a **5-6 year useful life**, mirroring the replacement cycle of terrestrial chips.
    *   **Reliability Data:** The H100 GPU currently in orbit has reported zero restart failures, suggesting that GPU workloads (which are stochastic) are naturally resilient to minor space-induced errors.

## Scaling with SpaceX Starship
*   **Launch Capacity:** SpaceX’s Starship is the primary catalyst. Johnston anticipates Starship will eventually launch **10MW of compute capacity per flight** using a "Pez dispenser" deployment mechanism.
*   **Deployment Velocity:** Once Starship reaches a high flight cadence, Starcloud expects to deploy several gigawatts of new capacity monthly.
*   **Inference vs. Training:** Starcloud focuses on **AI inference** rather than frontier model training. Inference is less hindered by the speed-of-light latency (sub-50ms via Starlink) and represents the vast majority of future AI workloads.
*   **Business Model:** Starcloud aims to be the **"Equinix of Space,"** providing the "box" (power, cooling, and connectivity) while allowing hyperscalers or customers to provide their own chip architectures.

## Strategic Outlook and Market Predictions
*   **CapEx Shift:** Johnston predicts that within 10 years, close to **$1 trillion in annual CapEx** will flow toward space-based compute infrastructure.
*   **The "Space Force" Factor:** Security is managed via orbital velocity (moving at 27,000 km/h makes satellites harder to hit than stationary Earth targets) and protection from the U.S. Space Force.
*   **Initial Customers:** Early adoption is driven by **military and government sectors** needing to process high-bandwidth data (like Synthetic Aperture Radar) in-situ to bypass data downlink bottlenecks.
*   **Long-term Vision:** Johnston envisions a future where **99.9% of GDP** is tied to inference compute, potentially moving toward a "Dyson Sphere" level of energy and compute utilization.

> "Within 5 to 10 years at least half of all new compute capacity is being deployed in space for the energy... It just makes zero sense to continue building things on earth." — **Philip Johnston**

> "The marginal cost on every additional data center you add to the [terrestrial] grid goes up... In space, the marginal cost goes down for every additional unit because you're manufacturing at rate." — **Philip Johnston**

> "We are very quickly running up against constraints on where and how we can build new energy projects terrestrially... we're very rapidly plowing towards a brick wall." — **Philip Johnston**

briefings.title: How this CEO rose to lead a $1.7 trillion financial giant
briefings.tldr: Jenny Johnson, CEO of Franklin Templeton, is transforming the $1.7 trillion investment giant by blending a multigenerational legacy of long-term stewardship with aggressive "native" adoption of blockchain and AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Jenny Johnson, CEO of Franklin Templeton, is transforming the $1.7 trillion investment giant by blending a multigenerational legacy of long-term stewardship with aggressive "native" adoption of blockchain and AI. She emphasizes a leadership philosophy of "people, passion, purpose, and persistence" to navigate market volatility and technological disruption.

## Leadership and Family Legacy
*   **Generational Stewardship:** As a third-generation leader, Johnson manages $1.7 trillion in assets—a massive leap from the $2.5 million firm her father took over.
    *   She highlights that "third-generation failure" is common because of a lack of motivation; she avoids this by instilling family values like hard work and integrity.
    *   **External Validation:** Despite being family, Johnson underwent a rigorous external board review before being named CEO to ensure she was the best candidate.
*   **The "Four Ps" Philosophy:** Johnson centers her leadership on four core pillars:
    *   **People:** Selecting the right talent to allow the organization to scale.
    *   **Passion:** Finding joy in the work so it doesn't feel like a burden.
    *   **Purpose:** Rallying the team around financial milestones (e.g., retirement, education) rather than just beating an index.
    *   **Persistence:** Staying the course through crises like the pandemic.
*   **The Power of Mentorship:** Her father, now 93, remains her primary influence. He taught her the importance of "taking care of the client" and the necessity of persistence, once using a cartoon of a frog refusing to be swallowed by a duck to illustrate the "never give up" mindset.

## Strategic Execution and Crisis Management
*   **Navigating the Pandemic:** Johnson became CEO just before the COVID-19 lockdowns and concurrently announced the acquisition of Legg Mason—effectively doubling the company’s size.
    *   **Remote Integration:** Due to travel restrictions, the firm had to conduct talent reviews and close the transaction via Zoom, ultimately finishing the deal two months early.
    *   **Early Tech Adoption:** A prior culture of "desktop video" (using Tandberg devices) gave the firm a competitive edge in transitioning to remote work compared to less tech-savvy peers.
*   **The "Long-Term" Advantage:** Johnson argues that family-controlled public companies can resist the pressure of quarterly earnings to make "big bets" on technologies that may not pay off for 5–7 years.

## The Technological Frontier: AI and Blockchain
*   **Blockchain and Tokenization:** Johnson is a vocal advocate for blockchain as a "source of truth" to replace aging financial infrastructure.
    *   **Cost Reduction:** Blockchain eliminates the need for expensive data reconciliation between firms and counterparties.
    *   **Native Innovation:** Franklin Templeton launched a money market fund built *natively* on-chain (rather than a "digital twin"), allowing for "atomic settlement" and interest calculated to the second.
*   **AI as a Force Multiplier:** Rather than fearing displacement, Johnson views AI as a tool to enhance human expertise.
    *   **Virtual Research Analyst:** The firm uses a tool that ingests their investment philosophy and historical trades to act as a "bias check" during committee meetings.
    *   **Advice for Workers:** She encourages employees to "own their careers" by becoming the most proficient users of AI tools, regardless of their seniority or coding background.

## Career Advice and Productivity Hacks
*   **Work-Life Balance (The "Five-Year Rule"):** When faced with a conflict between personal and professional obligations, Johnson asks: "Five years from now, which of these things is going to be more important?"
*   **Managing Jet Lag:** Johnson’s primary travel hack is to sync with the destination’s time zone the moment she steps on the plane, avoiding sleep aids to preserve REM sleep.
*   **Active Learning:** She recently spent a weekend attempting to learn coding via Claude and Replit to better understand the technology disrupting her industry, underscoring the need for "curiosity and openness."

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Take care of the client and the business takes care of itself." — **Jenny Johnson** (quoting her father)

> "It’s a little bit like when you drive a car... you don’t look right in front of the car, you look down the road. And when you look down the road, the car naturally stays where it needs to go. You’ve got to be focused on the longer-term picture while being aware of the noise in the shorter term." — **Jenny Johnson**

> "It’s being willing as a family to put your own ego aside and say who's better on behalf of the family to be the steward of this asset." — **Jenny Johnson**

> "The technology is not usually the limitation. It’s people’s willingness to change." — **Jenny Johnson**

briefings.title: How to bet on yourself (without venture capital)
briefings.tldr: William Hockey, founder of Column and co-founder of Plaid, argues that the modern venture capital model encourages "safe" entrepreneurship and consensus-driven thinking.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
William Hockey, founder of Column and co-founder of Plaid, argues that the modern venture capital model encourages "safe" entrepreneurship and consensus-driven thinking. By self-funding a nationally chartered bank and focusing on the "boring" infrastructure of the global US dollar, Hockey advocates for a high-risk, high-conviction model of specialist building that prioritizes long-term profitability and national security interests over the "VC hamster wheel."

## Rejecting the "VC Hamster Wheel"
* **The Heroin of Venture Capital:** Hockey describes VC funding as a "heroin-like" addiction where founders optimize for the next fundraise rather than long-term product viability. This leads to "windy" business paths where strategies shift to follow trends like AI or stablecoins just to secure capital.
* **Extreme Founder Risk:** 
    * Hockey funded Column by pledging over $1 billion in Plaid shares to secure a $70 million loan to buy a bank, nearly facing bankruptcy and margin calls three times in the process.
    * He argues that Silicon Valley has de-risked the founder role too much, attracting people who want the "founder" resume item without the "raw intensity" of potential failure.
* **Employee Equity and Liquidity:**
    * **Annual Tenders:** Column uses 25% of its earnings every year to buy back shares from employees, providing predictable liquidity that traditional startups lack.
    * **Anti-Dilution:** Because the company avoids external funding rounds, employees face zero dilution, making a 1% stake in Column significantly more valuable than 1% in a heavily diluted VC-backed firm.

## The Strategic Moat of "Boring" Problems
* **The Specialist Advantage:** Value is found in deep, unglamorous niches that "Gemini deep research" cannot solve. Hockey emphasizes becoming the world’s leading expert in "confusing, boring-sounding" areas.
    * **Extreme Research:** Hockey studied 2,000-page histories of 19th-century Japanese and Chinese banking to find single product ideas that create millions in leverage.
* **Software Company + Bank:** Column is a software company that owns its own regulatory rails.
    * Unlike traditional "BaaS" (Banking-as-a-Service) providers that sit on top of other banks, Column is the bank.
    * 90% of revenue comes from software fees (API calls), not the interest rate "spread" typical of traditional banking.
* **Customer Longevity:** In financial services, customers like Ramp, Brex, and Wise pay for safety and longevity. Profitability is a feature that proves the company can be a "15-year partner" without relying on a VC’s investment committee.

## Emerging Markets as Innovation Labs
* **The Silicon Valley Consensus Problem:** Silicon Valley and Beijing are the two most consensus-oriented places in the world. Elites build software for other elites, losing touch with how "everyday America" or the rest of the world operates.
* **The "Kinshasa" Perspective:** 
    * Hockey frequently visits emerging markets like the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to observe how founders build under extreme constraints.
    * **Leapfrogging:** Just as China skipped laptops for mobile, emerging markets are leapfrogging Western financial services. For example, Kaspi in Kazakhstan and Rawbank in the DRC offer integrated vertical apps (paying taxes, renewing licenses) that far exceed the utility of US banking apps.
* **The Dollar as a Global OS:** The US dollar is most critical in "implicitly dollarized" emerging markets where local central banks are untrusted. These regions often need US financial infrastructure more than developed European markets do.

## The US Dollar as National Security
* **Sanctions Before Missiles:** Hockey views the US dollar as a primary national security asset. Controlling the global financial OS allows the US to enforce its will through sanctions—collapsing an enemy's trade ability—before ever putting "boots on the ground."
* **Infrastructure vs. Implementation:** 
    * Contrary to the narrative that US financial tech is "built on cobalt," Hockey asserts the Federal Reserve's underlying technology is actually quite robust and capable of 24/7 instant settlement.
    * The friction in the system (e.g., banks being closed on weekends) is a result of **business model constraints** (staffing, fraud protection for the vulnerable) rather than a lack of fundamental technology.

## AI and the Future of Value Accrual
* **Distribution Over Technology:** Value will not accrue to "AI companies" but to those with massive distribution and brand moats. 
* **The Beneficiaries:** 
    * Inefficient legacy brands with high headcount costs are the biggest potential winners of AI, as they can use the technology to drastically cut operational costs.
    * **Fraud Detection:** AI’s greatest contribution to fintech will be matching human-level fraud detection instantly. This will allow banks to remove the "protection friction" that currently slows down money movement for everyone to protect a small percentage of vulnerable users.

> "I think the most important thing you should do is say... what does my margin profile look like? What is my revenue growth over time? And how should I find a capital structure that matches that? The venture model is built off the fact that you can make a company like an ATM... that’s not the case with most markets." — **William Hockey**

> "Silicon Valley is not a popular place... our ability to actually build software or have ideas or perspectives that really resonate is probably at the low point in the entire time I’ve been here. Elites end up building software for elites." — **William Hockey**

> "I think that the good founders bet on themselves and take an extreme amount of risk... When there’s literally only one door in front of you, you don’t have a choice. You have to go in. And that fear creates another part of you." — **William Hockey**

briefings.title: ICYMI: President Trump & JD Vance Take Questions About The Iran War In The Oval Office

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: President Trump and Vice President JD Vance detailed the near-total decimation of Iran’s military and leadership following targeted strikes, while concurrently launching a massive domestic "fraud task force" to recoup billions in misappropriated funds from U.S. cities.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump and Vice President JD Vance detailed the near-total decimation of Iran’s military and leadership following targeted strikes, while concurrently launching a massive domestic "fraud task force" to recoup billions in misappropriated funds from U.S. cities.

## Military Strategy and the Iranian Conflict
*   **Operational Success:** President Trump claimed that U.S. military actions have effectively neutralized Iran’s offensive capabilities.
    *   **Asset Destruction:** Iran has reportedly lost its entire navy, air force, and anti-aircraft weaponry, and is down to roughly 8% of its original missile and drone inventory.
    *   **B-2 Stealth Bombers:** Trump praised the B-2’s role in the conflict, noting it is the only aircraft capable of carrying a 200,000-pound payload and was essential in destroying Iran’s "nuclear dust" and underground facilities.
*   **Leadership Vacuum:** Trump stated that two to three layers of Iranian leadership have been "extinguished," including the primary successors to the Supreme Leader.
*   **Conflict Timeline:** The President signaled that while he does not want a long war, the conflict will not end this week, though it will be "wrapped up soon" to ensure Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon.
*   **Retaliatory Surprises:** Trump admitted that experts were shocked when Iran launched thousands of missiles at neutral neighbors like the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait during the escalation.

## Domestic Integrity and the "Fraud Czar"
*   **Task Force Mandate:** Vice President JD Vance embraced the title of "fraud czar," leading a task force designed to root out systemic corruption and "country-changing" amounts of stolen tax dollars.
*   **Minnesota Medicaid Crackdown:** Vance confirmed that the administration has halted Medicaid payments to Minnesota. 
    *   **Enforcement:** Dr. Mehmet Oz is working with local authorities to investigate pervasive fraud, specifically citing concerns regarding the Somali community and the flow of illicit cash through the Minneapolis airport.
*   **Law Enforcement Integration:** The task force will utilize the DOJ to pursue criminal prosecutions. Trump and Vance characterized much of the systemic fraud in New York, Chicago, and California as criminal rather than merely administrative.
*   **Resource Allocation:** Trump argued that recovering these funds would allow for substantial tax lowers for the American public and turn the national deficit into a "profitable country."

## Allied Relations and Global Contributions
*   **Burden Sharing:** Trump expressed deep disappointment with NATO allies and Asian partners (Japan, South Korea, China) for their lack of military or financial support during the Iran operation.
    *   **Energy Protection:** Trump noted that while Japan and China receive over 90% of their energy through the Strait of Hormuz, the U.S. is bearing the full cost and risk of securing the waterway.
*   **Critique of the UK:** Trump specifically criticized the United Kingdom’s Prime Minister for hesitating to send minesweepers and ships until after the U.S. had already secured the region.
*   **Military Presence Abroad:** The President questioned the continued deployment of 45,000–50,000 troops in Germany, Japan, and South Korea if those nations refuse to assist in U.S.-led security operations.

## Legislative and Social Priorities
*   **Save America Act:** Trump is pushing for a Senate vote on a package that includes:
    *   **Voter Integrity:** Mandatory photo ID, proof of citizenship for voting, and the elimination of mail-in ballots.
    *   **Cultural Issues:** Federal bans on "transgender mutilation" (gender-affirming surgeries for minors) and men participating in women's sports.
*   **Partisan Unity:** Trump criticized Republican "independents" for failing to stick together like Democrats, whom he described as "glue" when voting on party-line issues.
*   **DHS Funding:** Trump blamed Democrats for a lack of funding for the Department of Homeland Security, claiming that 80% of the anti-terrorism task force is currently working without pay.

## Future Foreign Policy: Cuba and China
*   **China Excursion:** Trump noted he has requested a delay for his planned trip to Beijing, stating it is imperative he remains in Washington until the Iranian conflict is further stabilized.
*   **The "Taking" of Cuba:** Trump described Cuba as a "failed nation" and suggested the U.S. is currently in a position to "free" or "take" the island in some form. 
    *   **Economic Potential:** He characterized the island as a high-value landscape for tourism and entrepreneurship once the "violent leadership" is addressed.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "It's money first, power second. A lot of people say power first, no. It's money first, power second... This type of fraud, the corruption, is the type of thing that can shred the fabric of a nation." — **President Donald Trump**

> "I think all of us, whether you're a Democrat or Republican, should pray for [the Iran operation's] success and pray for the safety of our troops... I trust President Trump to get the job done... and make sure that the mistakes of the past aren't repeated." — **Vice President JD Vance**

> "If you believe that Iran should not have a nuclear weapon, then you have to absolutely love what I've done because in two weeks we have decimated them. They have no navy, they have no air force, they have no anti-aircraft weapons. They have no leadership." — **President Donald Trump**

> "I don't want them anymore. I don't want them after we win, I want them before we start. I don't need your aircraft carriers after we've already won." — **President Donald Trump** (referencing the UK Prime Minister)

briefings.title: The Career Advice That Ruins Lives (And What Actually Works) - Bill Gurley

people.name: Anthony Scaramucci
people.role: Founder and Managing Partner, SkyBridge Capital

briefings.tldr: True career security in the age of AI comes from pursuing deep "fascination" rather than traditional safety, as obsessive curiosity fuels the continuous learning and high energy required to reach the top 1% of any field.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** True career security in the age of AI comes from pursuing deep "fascination" rather than traditional safety, as obsessive curiosity fuels the continuous learning and high energy required to reach the top 1% of any field.

## The Psychology of Career Regret
* **Regrets of Inaction:** Citing Daniel Pink’s research, Gurley emphasizes that humans easily forgive themselves for "action mistakes" (failed ventures), but are haunted by "boldness regrets"—the things they never tried.
    * **Statistical Dissatisfaction:** Surveys by Wharton and SurveyMonkey indicate that 60% to 70% of college-educated professionals would start their careers over differently if given the chance.
* **The "Use It or Lose It" Proposition:** Young people often view time as infinite, but by age 40 or 50, the weight of wasted time becomes heavy. Gurley argues that since most people will work 80,000 hours in their life, doing anything other than what they love is a massive strategic error.
* **Fascination vs. Passion:** Gurley prefers the term "fascination" (borrowed from Jerry Seinfeld) over the cliché of "passion." 
    * **The Litmus Test:** Fascination is defined by a natural desire to study the history, nuance, and greats of a field during your free time.

## Mastery Through "Honing the Craft"
* **The Bob Dylan Model:** Gurley describes Bob Dylan as a "historian" of folk music who studied the genre more intensely than anyone else before finding success.
    * **Continuous Learning:** Elite success is a "vector" of continuous learning. If studying your field feels like an alternative to watching Netflix, you are in the right lane.
* **The Artisan Approach:** In an AI-dominated world, rote knowledge is no longer a competitive advantage. 
    * **Finding the Edge:** Success now requires acting like a craftsman—studying the nuance and "edge" of a field where AI models lack data. 
    * **Mark Cuban’s AI Divide:** Gurley cites Cuban’s observation that there are two types of people: those who use Large Language Models (LLMs) to learn faster, and those who use them to avoid learning.

## Strategic Career Principles
* **Proactive Peer Groups:** Gurley argues that the "lone wolf" mentality is a mistake. He advocates for creating a formal peer group of people on the same "rung of the ladder."
    * **Shared Horsepower:** A trusted peer group provides shared learning, access to combined networks, and emotional support during the inevitable "bad days."
* **Go to the Epicenter:** For specific industries, geography remains a critical multiplier. 
    * **The Geographic Nexus:** If you are serious about a field, move to its epicenter (e.g., Silicon Valley for tech, New York for finance). This "nexus" accelerates every other principle of success.
* **The "Don't Half-Ass It" Rule:** Referencing Matthew McConaughey’s father, Gurley notes that choosing a dream career isn't about taking the easy way out; it is a "responsibility" to apply total effort.

## Advice for Young Professionals
* **The Risk of "Safe" Jobs:** Traditional "safe" paths are increasingly vulnerable to AI. The most "resourceful" version of a person only emerges when they are working on something they are passionate about.
* **Planning Over Paralysis:** For those with financial constraints or debt, Gurley recommends using "scenario planning" and AI tools to build a five-step game plan before taking the leap.
* **Resourcefulness over Fear:** Passion and fascination provide the "rocket fuel" necessary to overcome the fear of jumping off the cliff and "building the airplane on the way down."

***

> "The thing you never tried is the thing that eats at you as you get older." — **Bill Gurley**

> "I would argue the safest thing you could possibly do is find a career in something that you're totally fascinated with... Everything gets easier and you get energy rather than it costing you energy." — **Bill Gurley**

> "There are two types of people in the world: those that use LLMs to learn faster and even more, and those that use LLMs to avoid learning." — **Mark Cuban (quoted by Bill Gurley)**

> "Relax, none of us are getting out of here alive." — **Mel Brooks (quoted by Anthony Scaramucci)**

briefings.title: The Investor Behind a16z’s America First Push On Dealing With the Pentagon ‘Where Bits Meet Atoms’
briefings.tldr: David Ulevitch, head of Andreessen Horowitz’s $1.776 billion "American Dynamism" fund, details a strategic shift in Silicon Valley toward "heavy" industries—defense, energy, and manufacturing—where advanced software can disrupt legacy government contractors.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
David Ulevitch, head of Andreessen Horowitz’s $1.776 billion "American Dynamism" fund, details a strategic shift in Silicon Valley toward "heavy" industries—defense, energy, and manufacturing—where advanced software can disrupt legacy government contractors. The core thesis posits that private venture capital can solve national security and infrastructure challenges more efficiently than traditional government-funded R&D by applying Silicon Valley’s high-speed, high-automation "bits meet atoms" approach.

## The "American Dynamism" Investment Thesis
*   **Target Sectors:** The fund focuses on categories serving the national interest, including defense, aerospace, energy resilience, supply chain, public safety, and domestic manufacturing.
*   **"Bits Meet Atoms":** Ulevitch defines the strategy as investing in the intersection of advanced software and physical hardware. 
    *   **Technological Shift:** The goal is to replace expensive, "exquisite" hardware with commodity hardware driven by sophisticated software (e.g., using phone optics and software to replace $25,000 vacuum-tube night vision systems).
*   **Market Durability:** While "capital-light" SaaS models are facing devaluation due to AI, Ulevitch argues that hardware-heavy businesses with high automation and verticalized supply chains offer high-margin, unconstrained upside.

## Disrupting the Defense Industrial Base
*   **Critique of Legacy Primes:** Ulevitch argues that major incumbents (the "Primes") are disincentivized to move fast or lower costs because their profit margins are often baked into "cost-plus" contracts where going over budget increases total profit.
*   **Economic Asymmetry:** Current military engagements highlight a cost crisis; the U.S. is using multi-million dollar Patriot missiles to intercept $250,000 Iranian-style drones. 
    *   **Startup Solution:** Startups like Anduril focus on high-rate, low-cost production using the "Elon philosophy" where the factory itself is the primary product.
*   **Procurement Shift:** Ulevitch advocates for a model where the government stops funding endless R&D and instead buys finished commercial products that meet specific capability specs, shifting the R&D risk to venture capitalists.

## AI, Ethics, and the "God Complex"
*   **The OpenAI/Anthropic Conflict:** Addressing the controversy regarding AI companies working with the Pentagon, Ulevitch views the choice as a "sorting algorithm" for talent.
*   **Opposition to "Extrajudicial" Decisions:** Ulevitch criticizes CEOs who refuse to sell to the government based on personal moral objections, calling it a "god complex." 
    *   **The Argument:** Private citizens lack the classified intelligence (satellite imagery, wiretaps) necessary to make better tactical decisions than the chain of command. 
    *   **Smart Weapons:** He argues AI will make weapons "smarter," allowing them to distinguish between a school bus and a tank more accurately than humans, thereby reducing collateral damage.

## Energy Abundance and Infrastructure
*   **Nuclear Renaissance:** The fund is heavily invested in nuclear energy (e.g., Radiant), viewing it as the cleanest and safest technology for meeting the "insatiable thirst" for power driven by AI data centers and EVs.
*   **Regulatory Acceleration:** AI is being used to drastically reduce the time needed to process complex regulatory and transport permits for nuclear facilities.
*   **The Venn Diagram of Security:** Ulevitch argues that energy, space, and defense are now inseparable; without domestic energy abundance and space-based communications, national security is impossible.

## Scaling Venture Capital to Trillion-Dollar Outcomes
*   **Outcome Potential:** Ulevitch pushes back against critics who say VC doesn't scale to heavy industry, citing SpaceX as a potential trillion-dollar outcome.
*   **The Capital Stack:** While VCs take the early equity risk, these companies eventually utilize private credit and real estate financing to build massive factories and data centers.
*   **Public Safety and Surveillance:** Defending investments like Flock Safety (license plate readers), Ulevitch argues that the benefit of solving crimes outweighs privacy concerns, noting that most privacy violations occur via data brokers and cell phones rather than transparent public safety tools.

> "The American Dynamism fund is a fund... focused on investing in companies that we say serve the national interest... it is where atoms meet bits, which historically has not been in vogue for the venture capital industry." — **David Ulevitch**

> "I actually think [the decision to work with government] is a sorting algorithm... there’s other people that say, 'we elect leaders, the leaders make laws, there’s lots of oversight... and I trust that democratic system.'" — **David Ulevitch**

> "If I had to bet on which end of the barbell will get to very high rates of production more quickly, is it the legacy incumbent primes who lack the institutional knowledge or appetite to move very, very fast, or the startups who have just survived an entire period of life of not dying? I would make that bet every single day of the week." — **David Ulevitch**

briefings.title: Two Legendary Founders: Travis Kalanick & Michael Dell Live from Austin, Texas
briefings.tldr: Travis Kalanick officially exits stealth mode with "Atoms," a company focused on automating the physical world across food, mining, and robotics, while Michael Dell details Dell Technologies' $50B pivot toward AI infrastructure and a landmark $6.25B gift to seed investment accounts for 25 million American children.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Travis Kalanick officially exits stealth mode with "Atoms," a company focused on automating the physical world across food, mining, and robotics, while Michael Dell details Dell Technologies' $50B pivot toward AI infrastructure and a landmark $6.25B gift to seed investment accounts for 25 million American children.

## Travis Kalanick: Exiting Stealth with "Atoms"
*   **Company Rebrand:** Kalanick’s holding company, City Storage Systems, has officially rebranded to **Atoms**. After years in stealth with thousands of employees, the company is focusing on "digitizing the physical world" by treating atoms like bits.
*   **The Atoms-Based Computer:** Kalanick views the physical economy through three core computing resources:
    *   **Manufacturing (CPU):** Manipulating atoms.
    *   **Real Estate (Storage):** Storing atoms.
    *   **Logistics (Network):** Moving atoms from point A to point B.
*   **Sector Diversification:**
    *   **Food Infrastructure:** Operates brands like CloudKitchens (US) and Kitchen Valley (Korea). The goal is to make prepared food delivery as cheap as grocery shopping.
    *   **Mining Automation:** Atoms is in the final stages of acquiring **Pronto**, a San Francisco-based company automating mining equipment. Kalanick aims to make mines more productive and safety-efficient in inhospitable locations.
    *   **Robotics:** Development of "wheelbases for robots" to provide movement for specialized, non-humanoid industrial robots.
*   **Physical AI Stack:** Kalanick identifies Tesla as the current leader in this space, noting that the "Physical AI stack" requires mastery of land development, chemistry, and manufacturing, not just software.

## The Great Migration: Why Founders are Choosing Texas
*   **California’s Decline:** Kalanick and Dell discussed the "mourning process" of leaving California. Kalanick described California’s current state as "weird," citing a degradation of "truth and justice"—which he calls the "immune system for society."
*   **Austin as the Future:** Both founders praised Austin for its pro-growth, low-tax environment.
    *   **Dell’s Perspective:** Texas now hosts four of the ten largest U.S. cities and produces one out of every ten children born in the U.S.
    *   **The "Wellspring":** Michael Dell credits the University of Texas as the foundational "wellspring" for the region's tech explosion.
*   **Regulatory Speed:** Michael Dell highlighted that Texas "lets you build," contrasting the ease of constructing data centers and factories in Texas versus the years of bureaucratic hurdles in California.

## Michael Dell: The $50B AI Infrastructure Pivot
*   **Scale of AI Demand:** Dell Technologies is on track for **$140B in annual revenue**, driven largely by a massive shift to AI infrastructure. Dell’s AI server business has grown from $2B to an estimated **$50B annually**.
*   **The "AI Factory" Model:** Dell has deployed over **4,000 "AI Factories"** for enterprises. He notes that the barrier to AI adoption is rarely technology, but rather "culture, leadership, and courage" to disrupt existing business models.
*   **Inference at the Edge:** Dell predicts a rebalancing where intelligence moves closer to where data is created.
    *   **Sovereign AI:** Governments and large enterprises want to keep data private and local rather than sending it to public clouds.
    *   **Cost Efficiency:** "The lowest cost token is generated right where the data is," such as on the device or local server, to avoid the high "bill shock" of public clouds.
*   **Paradigm Shift:** Dell describes the transition from 60 years of "calculating computing" to a new era of "thinking machines" that accelerate scientific discovery and problem-solving.

## "Invest America": A New Social Contract
*   **Historic Philanthropy:** Michael and Susan Dell announced a **$6.25B gift** to seed investment accounts for **25 million children** in zip codes with median incomes under $150,000.
*   **401k from Birth:** The Invest America Act creates a "401k from birth" for every American child born after **January 1, 2027**.
    *   **Account Structure:** Each child receives a "Trump account" (stapled to their Social Security card) with an initial government contribution, which can then be matched by private philanthropists and parents.
    *   **Ownership Society:** Brad Gerstner noted the goal is to reconnect the 70% of Americans who feel "left behind" by the stock market to the American Dream by making them owners of the S&P 500 from infancy.
*   **The Vision:** The program aims to move **$5 trillion** into the hands of American families over 15 years through compounding growth, bypassing traditional government "crony structures."

## Notable Quotes
> **Travis Kalanick:** "Truth and justice are the immune system for society. When the immune system is suppressed, all the social ills flare up."

> **Michael Dell:** "The barrier to technology adoption is not technology. It's culture and leadership and courage—the willingness to change and disrupt yourself."

> **Brad Gerstner:** "This is Social Security 2.0. It’s the biggest change to the social contract in America in 50 years... giving kids a shot to be an owner in the upside of America."

> **Travis Kalanick:** "If you can get a meal prepared and delivered so efficiently that it starts to approach the cost of the grocery store, you do to the kitchen what Uber did to the car."

briefings.title: Weekly Washington Policy Pulse: Iran, Basel III, Stablecoins, Warsh (March 16, 2026) | Balance...
briefings.tldr: President Trump is pushing for a "coalition of the willing" to secure the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating Iran tensions, while the financial sector prepares for the "Super Bowl" of regulation with the formal Basel III Endgame proposal this Thursday.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump is pushing for a "coalition of the willing" to secure the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating Iran tensions, while the financial sector prepares for the "Super Bowl" of regulation with the formal Basel III Endgame proposal this Thursday.

## Geopolitics and the Iran Conflict
*   **Strait of Hormuz Escorts:** President Trump has called for an international "coalition of the willing" (including China, the UK, Japan, South Korea, and Australia) to provide naval escorts for tankers.
    *   **International Response:** Current feedback is muted; Japan, Australia, and Germany have indicated they have no immediate plans or have not received formal requests.
*   **US-China Relations:** Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt suggested President Trump may delay his planned summit with President Xi Jinping, stating the President will not leave U.S. soil "at times of war."
    *   **Trade Negotiations:** U.S. and Chinese officials are currently in Paris negotiating tariffs, with outcomes expected shortly.
*   **Defense Supplemental Funding:** The Pentagon is reportedly seeking ~$50 billion in an Iranian supplemental defense bill. 
    *   **Legislative "Christmas Tree":** Congressional committees are already looking to attach riders, including $15 billion in farm aid and $20 billion for disaster insurance. The final package could reach $100–$200 billion, though floor action is unlikely before summer.

## Banking and Financial Regulation
*   **Basel III Endgame:** The formal proposal is expected this Thursday, kicking off a 90-day comment period.
    *   **Capital Requirements:** Requirements for operational and market risk are expected to increase, while credit risk for mortgages may decrease to incentivize bank originations.
*   **G-SIB Surcharge:** A "Method 2" tweak to the G-SIB surcharge is anticipated, which could provide approximately $32 billion in capital relief for the six largest "Global Systemically Important Banks" (JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup).
*   **Prediction Markets:** The CFTC issued guidance classifying most prediction markets as "swaps" under the Commodities Exchange Act. 
    *   **Rulemaking Timeline:** A formal rule is not expected to be finalized until mid-2027, making it difficult for future administrations to quickly reverse the stance via simple guidance.

## Digital Assets and Crypto Policy
*   **Stablecoin Regulation:** The Senate Banking Committee is expected to intensify work on a "clarity draft" regarding stablecoin yields in April.
*   **OCC "Genius Act" Implementation:** The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has proposed rules requiring stablecoin issuers to hold 100% high-quality liquid assets.
    *   **Yield Ban Controversy:** The OCC proposal includes a provision that would prohibit "handshake agreements" between issuers and third-party platforms offering reward programs, a move heavily opposed by the crypto industry.
*   **CBDC Ban:** The Senate-passed housing bill includes a ban on a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) through 2030, though House Republicans are pushing for a permanent ban.

## Congressional and Administrative Outlook
*   **Housing Legislation:** The "21st Century for Road Housing Act" has moved to the House after passing the Senate.
    *   **Institutional Investors:** A contentious provision would require single-family REITs to dispose of rental properties within seven years, which critics argue will stifle new construction.
*   **The SAFE Act:** President Trump has signaled he will not sign any legislation until this voter identification bill passes. 
    *   **Filibuster Standoff:** Senator John Thune (R-SD) lacks the 60 votes required for passage, but is expected to move through procedural motions to demonstrate effort to the White House.
*   **Fed Chair Nomination:** Senator Tom Tillis continues to block Kevin Warsh’s nomination for Federal Reserve Chair. 
    *   **Interim Leadership:** If the nomination remains stalled by May, Governor Miron may step in as acting Chair.

> "At times of war, the president is not going to leave U.S. soil." — **Karoline Leavitt**, White House Press Secretary (as paraphrased by Nathan Dean)

> "This Thursday, it's like the Super Bowl for bank investors. Uh the Basel III Endgame is finally being proposed." — **Nathan Dean**, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Policy Analyst

> "I think the White House is going to have to go over to the House and knock some heads into Pluto." — **Senator John Kennedy** (on the 21st Century for Road Housing Act)

briefings.title: Why Scale Will Not Solve AGI | Vishal Misra - The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: While LLMs are mathematically precise Bayesian inference engines, they are limited by their inability to learn continuously (plasticity) and their reliance on correlation over causation; true AGI requires a shift from pattern matching (Shannon entropy) to causal simulation (Kolmogorov complexity).
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** While LLMs are mathematically precise Bayesian inference engines, they are limited by their inability to learn continuously (plasticity) and their reliance on correlation over causation; true AGI requires a shift from pattern matching (Shannon entropy) to causal simulation (Kolmogorov complexity).

## The LLM as a "Giant Matrix"
*   **Mathematical Abstraction:** Vishal Misra describes an LLM as a gargantuan, sparse matrix where every possible prompt is a row and the distribution over the vocabulary (e.g., 50,000 tokens) forms the columns.
    *   **Sparse Distribution:** Because most token combinations are gibberish, the matrix is extremely sparse. LLMs act as a compressed representation of this "true" probability distribution.
*   **Bayesian Updating:** In-context learning (ICL) is the process of the model updating its "beliefs" in real-time. 
    *   **Evidence-Based Inference:** As a user provides examples in a prompt, the model shifts its posterior probability distribution. 
    *   **Domain-Specific Example:** Misra proved this by creating a cricket-specific language (DSL) that the model had never seen; by providing few-shot examples, the model’s probability of producing the correct "nonsense" tokens moved toward 100%.

## The "Bayesian Wind Tunnel" Experiments
*   **Proven Precision:** To counter critics who argued "anything can be Bayesian," Misra’s team created a "Bayesian wind tunnel"—a controlled environment where models were given tasks with analytically calculable solutions.
    *   **Architectural Performance:** Transformers matched the precise mathematical Bayesian posterior down to $10^{-3}$ bits of accuracy.
    *   **Hierarchy of Architectures:** The research found that Transformers are the most capable Bayesian engines, followed by Mamba. LSTMs were only partially successful, and MLPs (Multi-Layer Perceptrons) failed the tasks entirely.
*   **Geometric Signatures:** By examining the gradients of frontier open-weight models, Misra found that the same mathematical geometries observed in small experimental models persist in massive production LLMs.

## Fundamental Barriers to AGI
*   **Lack of Plasticity:** Unlike the human brain, which remains plastic throughout its life, LLM weights are frozen after training. 
    *   **Memory Limitations:** While LLMs "learn" during a conversation context, they "forget" everything once the context window is cleared. AGI requires "continual learning" without "catastrophic forgetting."
*   **Correlation vs. Causation:** Misra argues that deep learning is currently trapped in "Shannon entropy" (predicting the next token via association) rather than "Kolmogorov complexity" (finding the shortest causal program to explain data).
    *   **The Simulation Gap:** Humans use causal models to simulate the world (e.g., dodging a thrown pen). Current LLMs only match patterns and lack this internal "simulator."
*   **The Consciousness Debate:** Misra rejects the idea of LLM consciousness, describing them as "grains of silicon doing matrix multiplication."
    *   **Objective Functions:** Humans are driven by "survival and reproduction," whereas LLMs are driven solely by "next-token accuracy."

## The "Einstein Test" for Intelligence
*   **The Manifold Limitation:** LLMs are excellent at navigating existing "manifolds" of data (the space of human knowledge). However, they cannot yet create *new* manifolds.
*   **Theory of Relativity Challenge:** Misra proposes a benchmark for AGI: train an LLM on physics data only from before 1911. 
    *   **The Goal:** If the model can independently derive the Theory of General Relativity—rejecting existing Newtonian axioms to create a new representation of space-time—it has reached AGI.
    *   **Current Failure:** Current models treat anomalies as "noise" or outliers rather than using them to synthesize a more efficient, shorter "program" (Kolmogorov complexity) for the universe.

## Notable Quotes
> "Anthropic makes great products... But they are grains of silicon doing matrix multiplication. They don't have consciousness. They don't have an inner monologue... You can rule out their consciousness." — **Vishal Misra**

> "To get to what is called AGI, I think there are two things that need to happen. One is this plasticity... Secondly, we have to move from correlation to causation." — **Vishal Misra**

> "Einstein had to create a new manifold. If you just stuck with the old manifold of Newtonian physics, you would see these correlations, but you could not come up with a manifold that explained them." — **Vishal Misra**

> "I think deep learning is still in the Shannon entropy world; it has not crossed over to the Kolmogorov complexity and the causal world." — **Vishal Misra**
